issues.legal_issue: Capital value for a municipal rate assessed on a capital basis must be determined by the contractors’ method rather than by relying only on historic construction cost less depreciation.
material_facts: The dispute concerned the valuation of non-residential buildings belonging to a factory for a municipal property-rate assessment on a capital basis.
The company relied on historic book figures, while the lower courts used estimates based in part on the original construction cost and increases in building costs.
The courts below did not determine the value using the contractors’ method.
issues.conclusion: The lower courts used an incorrect method. Capital value must be determined using the contractors’ method, and the matter was remanded for that determination after the parties were given an opportunity to adduce evidence.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 73 of the Bombay Municipal Boroughs Act, 1925, a rate is a tax associated with annual or rateable value, and capital value may be used as a basis for working out that value. Under rule 4, the relevant properties were to be valued on a capital basis. Applying Patel Gordhandas Hargovindas v. Municipal Commissioner, Ahmedabad, the capital value could be determined by the contractors’ method: estimate construction cost, make deductions for age and obsolescence, estimate the land cost, apply the relevant market rate to the effective capital value, and consider whether the resulting annual amount reflects what a hypothetical tenant would pay. R. v. School Board for London was also referred to in connection with that method.

issues.legal_issue: Entries in a company’s balance sheet made under the prescribed accounting format are not, by themselves, reliable data for determining property capital value for a municipal rate.
material_facts: The company relied on figures in its audited balance sheets and accounts as the value of the properties.
The balance-sheet figures were prepared under a prescribed format that recorded original cost, additions and deductions, and depreciation.
The figures were accounting statements prepared for company reporting, rather than valuations of the properties for the rate assessment.
issues.conclusion: The balance-sheet figures could not be regarded as reliable data for determining the properties’ capital value for the assessment.
issues.legal_principle: Rule 5 required capital value to be determined on reliable data furnished by the relevant owner and, in the absence of such data, by the municipal chief officer or expert valuers. Section 211 and Schedule VI, Part I, of the Companies Act, 1956, required balance-sheet entries to be presented in a prescribed form; those entries, including original cost and depreciation, had no relevance as a measure of capital value for a municipal rate.

issues.definition: When a company relies on accounting entries recording cost and depreciation to value property in a municipal rating assessment, those entries are not reliable data for determining the property’s capital value.

issues.legal_issue: The established English rating meaning of an undefined term may guide interpretation of a similar local-tax statute when the statutes share a purpose and the local statute provides no contrary indication.
material_facts: The statute authorized a municipality to impose a rate but did not define the term “rate.”
The relevant local-tax legislation closely resembled English legislation and served the same purpose.
The court found no indication in the legislation that required a different meaning.
issues.conclusion: The English rating meaning could guide interpretation: a rate is associated with annual or rateable value, and capital value may be used as a basis for working out that value rather than being the tax base itself.
issues.legal_principle: The court applied Patel Gordhandas Hargovindas v. Municipal Commissioner, Ahmedabad, which examined English rating law and treated “rate” as a tax on net annual or rateable value, not on capital value itself, while permitting capital value to be used to work out annual value. Where Indian legislation closely resembles English legislation and has the same purpose, an undefined expression may receive the established English meaning unless the Indian statute indicates otherwise.
